correctness.rationale: Every binary word has a unique gap vector \((g_0,\ldots,g_A)\) with sum \(B\), where \(C=\sum_{j=1}^{A}j g_j\) and \(I=\sum_{j=1}^{A-1}g_j\). At fixed \(I=s\), the internal weighted weak compositions give \(z^s\) times a Gaussian binomial; the final gap ranges from zero to \(B-s\). For \(A\ge3\) and \(s\ge2\), internal weight sums fill \([s,(A-1)s]\), and adjacent shifts by \(A\) touch because \((A-2)s\ge A-1\), proving support \([s,AB-s]\). The \(A=2\) case has a parity restriction; \(s=0,1\) give modular holes. The standalone checker evaluated 12,825 words across 48 parameter pairs and 4,640 independent pattern tests. The infinite proof does not rely on finite testing.

value.rationale: The motivating problem is exact single-pattern occurrence probability inside a fixed binary Parikh-matrix language, a quantity addressed only approximately for arbitrary fixed patterns in the cited recent paper. This result computes the entire conditional distribution for every member of the infinite family \(ab^t a\) and classifies all attainable internal-span values, including a sharp \(A=2\) parity versus \(A\ge3\) interval transition and a modulo-\(A\) obstruction at counts zero and one. The natural invariant directly determines occurrence/avoidance for all \(t\), rather than a contrived coefficient slice or a routine restatement of the Gaussian marginal.
